newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU presses U.S. to change telecoms rules.
newsitem.headline: EU presses U.S. to change telecoms rules.

text.p: The European Union has asked Washington to reconsider how it intends drafting new U.S. laws incorporating a global agreement on telecoms trade, saying current proposals discriminate against foreign operators.

A statement on Tuesday from the European Commission said the U.S. "risks violating its world trading obligations" if it continues with current proposals, and reserved the right to take action at the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

The dispute centres on Washington's interpretation of its obligations under a global telecoms deal agreed at the WTO in February which established guidelines for a so-called General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS).

The Commission, the EU's executive, said it is particularly concerned that the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) draft text on foreign participation in domestic telecoms maintains "broad and unclear public service factors" in deciding licence applications.

The FCC's proposals, the EU says, allows factors such as law enforcement, foreign policy or trade concerns to be taken into consideration as well as accepting the concept of "very high risk to competition" as reason for licence refusal.
The FCC proposals, first published on June 4, also dismantle an competition test for access to international services, a move the EU welcomes.
Nevertheless, the EU has asked Washington to reconsider the rest of the draft "otherwise the EU reserves the right to challenge those rules under the WTO", the statement said.
